transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for being here. I've asked you all to join me because the eighth-grade civics class has proposed an oral-history project that I need to review before approving. The project involves all 20 students conducting interviews with 20 community members, recording on personal phones, publishing the recordings on the school website, and retaining the files indefinitely. Before I can approve this, district policy requires me to compile findings from each of you regarding student eligibility, consent, recording technology, storage, and retention. I'd like to go through these areas systematically and hear your current findings so we can put together a complete approval packet. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. My roster review has identified a critical eligibility issue. Exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight students are eligible to conduct recorded interviews under district policy. The remaining twelve students have not completed the training and therefore may not conduct recorded interviews. Additionally, the approval file must include a training-verification record documenting which students have completed this requirement. This means the current draft plan, which calls for all 20 students to conduct interviews, will need to be revised.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. My family-consent review has identified an important issue regarding interviewee permissions. Five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive. The other 15 interviewees may be included in public publication. The approval packet must include a consent-exclusion record documenting which interviewees have not granted public publication permission. This means the current draft plan, which calls for publishing all 20 recordings on the public school website, will need to be revised to exclude those five recordings from public publication.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd now like to share my technology review findings. My review confirms that personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets for all interview recordings. Source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on personal devices or the public school website. Regarding retention, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — the current draft plan's proposal for indefinite retention is not permissible. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting the restricted-drive setup. This means the current draft plan will need to be revised in three key areas: recording devices, storage location, and retention timeline.
